title: Google Search campaign (RSA asset set, keywords, negatives, assets, guardrails)

gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, rating, review count, price, guarantee, CPC or search volume that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research. Gaps are written around (pick an angle the confirmed facts fully support); never an invention, never a placeholder in publishable copy; estimates are labelled as assumptions.

Limits: every headline ≤ 30 characters, description ≤ 90, display path ≤ 15, sitelink text ≤ 25 and sitelink description lines ≤ 35, callout and snippet value ≤ 25, PMax long headline ≤ 90 with one PMax description ≤ 60. Up to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions per RSA (15 and 4 unless the brief asks otherwise).

Editorial policy: no emoji, no exclamation mark in headlines, no ALL-CAPS words (acronyms excepted), no repeated punctuation, no phone numbers in ad text, no 'click here', no 'best'/'#1'/'leading' without a confirmed third-party source, no competitor trademarks in ad text.

Approval and budget: everything is drafted as paused for owner approval; total daily budgets × 30.4 do not exceed the stated monthly budget; no promised results (leads, rankings, ROI) and no guarantee the business hasn't confirmed.

anchors.1: Keyword absent from headlines, or one ad group covers unrelated intents.
anchors.3: Keyword in 1–2 headlines; ad groups roughly themed.
anchors.5: One intent per ad group; keyword in 3–4 headlines in varied natural forms; wording mirrors the landing-page H1.

anchors.1: Near-duplicate headlines (same keyword reordered) make up a third or more of the set.
anchors.3: Some variety but several headlines repeat the same angle or opening.
anchors.5: Each headline is a distinct reason to click across keyword, benefit, proof, offer, objection and CTA slots; no repeated openings.

anchors.1: Fragments that only make sense in a fixed order, or combinations that contradict or repeat.
anchors.3: Most combinations work; a few clash or repeat.
anchors.5: Any 3 headlines plus 2 descriptions read as one coherent, grammatical ad; descriptions are complete thoughts.

anchors.1: The ad promises an offer, price or service the landing page doesn't show, or all traffic goes to the homepage.
anchors.3: Same theme as the page but offer or wording differs.
anchors.5: Offer, price, terms and key words identical in ad and page; mismatches flagged with a page fix.

anchors.1: No negatives; broad match without conversion tracking.
anchors.3: Generic negative list; match types reasonable.
anchors.5: Business-specific negatives (jobs, DIY, free, wrong places and services, close variants spelled out), cross-negatives between ad groups, match types fit the data available.

anchors.1: No assets, or assets that repeat headlines.
anchors.3: Some sitelinks and callouts, generic or pointing to the same page.
anchors.5: 4+ sitelinks to distinct real pages, 4+ callouts adding new facts, a structured snippet, call/location/price assets where they apply, display paths with keyword and location or offer.

anchors.1: AI Max/PMax settings ignored; pins used by habit.
anchors.3: Settings mentioned without exclusions or reasons.
anchors.5: Text customization and Final URL expansion decided with reasons, URL exclusions and term exclusions listed, pins only for legally required text with 2–3 options.

anchors.1: Budget math missing, or a small budget split across many campaigns.
anchors.3: Budget stated but structure not matched to expected clicks.
anchors.5: Daily budget and expected clicks shown with assumptions labelled; structure, bid strategy, schedule and geography fit that volume; kill/scale rule tied to the owner's margin.

anchors.1: Generic or hype copy (Solutions, Trusted Partner, Unlock) that any rival could run.
anchors.3: Clear but mostly adjectives; few specifics.
anchors.5: Prices, places, times, brands and proof in plain words; unmistakably this business; no AI tells.
